theory.say:
• A lawsuit is a strict, court-run process; a missed deadline or misfiled document can get the case dismissed
• Pleadings: track service, set up files; discovery: gather data, prepare the client; trial prep: schedules, final medicals
• Discovery tools: Interrogatories (written questions under oath), Requests for Production (documents), Requests for Admission, RFAs (admit or deny)
• Every filing creates a docket entry, a line on the court's record; its clock runs whether or not the email arrived

frame.say:
• Phase one, pleadings: Complaint filed, defendant served, Answer back; track service and set up the files
• Phase two, discovery: interrogatories, requests for production, depositions (recorded interviews under oath); calendar every response, meet the client
• Phase three, trial prep: expert reports, motions, then trial or settlement; coordinate schedules, update final medicals
• Discovery takes most of a Case Manager's time; knowing the phase shows the week's work

theory.say:
• Defense goal: get the client to contradict himself, lose his temper or exaggerate; each costs credibility
• Broad questions are normal, not attacks
• Estimate vs. guess: an estimate rests on what he saw or felt; a guess claims what he couldn't know
• A deposition gathers information; nothing is won there, so the smallest target protects the case
• An objection is a formal flag on the record protecting the witness; answer, then stop

frame.say:
• Seven Golden Rules; 1: always tell the truth; a damaged case can be saved, a lied-about one can't
• 2 and 3: pause two full seconds, then answer in words: time to think, clean transcript, room to object
• 4 and 5: never guess; answer only what was asked, then stop; not knowing is a complete answer
• 6 and 7: hold the silence after answering; don't try to win
• General rules every client gets; none tells John what to say

rules.say:
• Four categories of defense questions: personal background, crash mechanics, medical history, daily life
• Medical history is underreported most; here, the 2021 low-back visits, which counsel usually already has
• "Is that all" can fence off the hand numbness; the complete record, not memory, is the full list
• Compound questions fold two facts into one yes; John can say a question is unclear
• On an objection John stops, then answers unless told not to; explain rules, never coach answers

why.say:
• After suit, Robert Smith's Answer attacks fault and mitigation

• Missed visits are failure to mitigate: claiming he didn't do enough to get better
• Fault can reduce or wipe out recovery; mitigation cuts only damages the missed care caused

theory.say:
• Comparative negligence splits fault; the injured person's share can reduce or bar recovery
• Pure, modified and contributory systems treat the same finding differently; the state's rule decides the money
• Record liability status, accepted, partial or denied, with its source
• Keep fault (the crash) and mitigation (later care) separate
• Counter-package: an index answering each defense claim with evidence usable in court

why.say:
• Dropped Case: a claim the firm stops pursuing before it resolves; John Doe's file never gets here
• Atty. Thorne talks to the client first; the letter only confirms it
• Withdrawal Letter: formal notice the lawyer-client relationship has ended
• Done carelessly, a drop confuses the client and exposes the firm; done right, the file proves everyone was told
• Red flag: a carrier letter saying Denise stopped treating. Only the client's letter carries the reason, in Atty. Thorne's words; elsewhere it's a defect

theory.say:
• A Dropped Case must be written up, closed out and proved
• Reasons: client stops answering or pulls out; fault can't be shown; no insurance money, or not enough
• Also: client can't finish treatment, new facts don't match, or no Health Plan to pay for care
• Pending Drop: the decision is made, letters not yet sent
• Proof, the receipts, logs and saved letters, protects the firm later

frame.say:
• Client letter: date, date of loss, reason in Atty. Thorne's words, his approved next step: speak to another attorney promptly
• Sent by the client's preferred method plus Certified Mail, which gives proof of delivery
• Carrier letter: date, client name, date of loss, claim number; says only the firm no longer represents the client
• Provider letter: the same, asking them to update records; both by email or fax, as CRM contact notes say
• The reason goes to the client only

rules.say:
• Six steps in order; 1, the gate: status Pending Drop and a note the client was told; either missing, nothing goes out
• 2: a Withdrawal Letter for every party over Atty. Thorne's signature, saved in Word and PDF; 3: send each by its method
• 4: annotate party, method, date, save the sent letter; 5: follow up on receipt
• 6: switch the status to Dropped and keep the proof
• An unresponsive client reaches this only through the No Contact Protocol

model.say:
• One rail, six steps; the gate's two ticks: Pending Drop and client told
• Three letters, client, carrier, provider, each in Word and PDF; sent by preferred method plus Certified Mail, or email or fax
• Annotate and save; follow up on the return receipt, acknowledgement and fax confirmation
• Status flips from Pending Drop to Dropped, proof kept; the follow-up is the step most often skipped

dodont.say:
• Do: check the gate before opening the template; Atty. Thorne decides in writing first
• Do: send the client's letter two ways, one with proof of arrival
• Don't: put the reason in a carrier's letter; don't switch to Dropped before every letter is out and logged
• Don't: tell the client the case is worthless; value is Atty. Thorne's conversation

theory.say:
• Net Sheet: where every dollar came from and where it goes, the receipt for the whole case
• Common fund doctrine: everyone paid from the recovery shares its cost, so lienholders share fees and costs; the basis for reductions
• Double-dipping trap: counting a dollar twice or paying a bill twice; carriers audit
• Fee transparency: each money stream carries its own fee, tracked separately
• Final Payoff Letter: a signed letter that this amount settles the bill in full; no letter, no check

why.say:
• Robert Smith is a party, so he must answer; the records custodian and witness Ruth Calloway don't, unless the court commands it
• That court command is a subpoena
• Serve it out of order, write it too broadly, or get records after discovery closes 05/28/2027, and evidence can be lost
• Red flag: "all records of any kind" invites a Motion to Quash. One subject, an exact date range, named record types; Atty. Thorne signs

theory.say:
• Subpoena Duces Tecum, "bring it with you": orders a non-party, like a hospital or employer, to produce documents
• Trial subpoena: orders a witness, like a treating doctor or police officer, to appear and testify
• "All records of any kind" invites a Motion to Quash, asking the court to cancel it
• Narrow model: ER records, triage notes, imaging, one client, the accident date only
• Order never changes: draft, notice opposing counsel, serve the custodian, track compliance
